question: What is 'typology' in biblical theology, and how does it differ from allegory?

choices.A: Typology sees OT persons, events, and institutions as genuine historical realities that also foreshadow (prefigure) their New Testament fulfillment; allegory treats OT narratives as coded spiritual meanings with less regard for historical reality
choices.B: Typology and allegory are identical methods — the same approach with different names
choices.C: Typology reads texts literally; allegory reads them spiritually, with no overlap possible
choices.D: Typology applies only to prophecy; allegory applies only to narrative

teaching.title: Typology vs. Allegory
teaching.body: Typology holds that OT 'types' (Greek: typos = pattern, impression) are real historical events or persons that God designed to prefigure their NT 'antitypes' (fulfillments). The historical reality of the type is essential — Adam is a real person who is also a 'type of the one to come' (Rom 5:14). Allegory (as practiced by Philo and later Origen) tends to read the surface narrative as a code for timeless spiritual truths, sometimes discarding the historical meaning. The Catechism teaches a fourfold sense of Scripture (literal, allegorical, moral, anagogical), but insists that the literal-historical sense is foundational (CCC 116).
